# powerdns_zone (Data Source)

Reads a zone the configuration does not manage.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A zone owned elsewhere — created by another team or by pdnsutil — whose
# records this configuration adds to.
data "powerdns_zone" "shared" {
  name = "example.com."
}

resource "powerdns_record" "ours" {
  zone   = data.powerdns_zone.shared.id
  name   = "service.example.com."
  type   = "A"
  ttl    = 300
  values = ["192.0.2.10"]
}

# record_count rather than the sets themselves: a zone with thousands of them
# would put all of them in state on every refresh.
output "size" {
  value = data.powerdns_zone.shared.record_count
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The zone to read. A trailing dot is added if absent.

### Read-Only

- `account` (String) Free-form owner label.
- `catalog` (String) The catalog zone this zone belongs to.
- `dnssec` (Boolean) Whether the zone is signed.
- `edited_serial` (Number) The serial a query would see, after SOA-EDIT.
- `id` (String) The canonical zone name.
- `kind` (String) `Native`, `Master`, `Slave`, `Producer` or `Consumer`.
- `masters` (List of String) Primary servers, for a `Slave` zone.
- `record_count` (Number) How many RRSets the zone holds. The sets themselves are not exposed: a zone with thousands of them would put all of them in state on every refresh, and `powerdns_record` is the way to address one.
- `serial` (Number) The SOA serial as stored.
- `soa_edit` (String) SOA-EDIT policy.
- `soa_edit_api` (String) SOA-EDIT-API policy.
